summary.oneLiner: Remsons delivered 20% YoY revenue growth in Q3FY26 driven by order wins in CV gear shifters, Stellantis North America ramp-up, and railway entry, with margin expansion on track toward 13-14% EBITDA by FY29 through higher-value systemization and export diversification — what matters is the structural shift from commodity cables to high-margin systems and global supply chain re-shoring benefits.

one-line thesis: Remsons delivered 20% YoY revenue growth in Q3FY26 driven by order wins in CV gear shifters, Stellantis North America ramp-up, and railway entry, with margin expansion on track toward 13-14% EBITDA by FY29 through higher-value systemization and export diversification — what matters is the structural shift from commodity cables to high-margin systems and global supply chain re-shoring benefits.
financial scorecard: revenue: +20% YoY (INR123cr Q3); EBITDA/margin: 12% (Q3), +11% (9M) — no one-offs; PAT (rptd): 4% (Q3), 4% (9M); PAT (normalized): ~6-7% (ex-early capex dilution); order book: INR500cr; net debt: 0.63x D/E — stable, no distress
guidance: revenue growth: FY27 INR520-570cr (ex-acquisition); margin: steady climb to 11-12% in FY27, 13-14% by FY29; order inflow: INR800-900cr pipeline; capex/commissioning: FY26 capex INR20-26cr; FY27 capex INR20cr+; railway facility commissioned; NCR expansion 20k sq.ft. in progress
order book & pipeline: INR500cr (current); INR800-900cr (2-3 year pipeline); includes INR60cr CV order (FY27 start), INR300cr+ Stellantis (FY27 ramp), INR12cr BEE Lighting (UK), INR3cr EGR sensor (Germany)
segment / subsidiary detail: Control Cables: 60%+ revenue; Gear Shifters/Push-Pull: INR60cr order (CV, 5-year); Railway: INR25-35cr revenue FY26; BEE Lighting: INR12cr order (UK, low-volume); EGR Sensors: INR3cr order (Germany); Brazil: early-stage, no revenue yet; Defense: INR10-15cr revenue FY25, incremental products in pipeline
growth verticals / optionality: Railway (INR25-35cr FY26, export potential); Brazil (tech partnership, 12-18mo lead time); Defense (long-cycle, Atmanirbhar alignment); Systemization (from components to integrated modules); US tariff advantage (INR40-50cr annual RFQ pipeline reactivated)
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin at 12% (Q3) — improvement driven by product mix shift (higher-value systems), not cost cuts; legacy commodity products still dominant but productivity improving; margin expansion to 13-14% by FY29 via systemization and export premiumization; no material raw material inflation pressure cited
capex / expansion: FY26: INR15-19cr spent; additional INR5-7cr expected in remaining 1.5 months; total FY26 capex: INR20-26cr; FY27: INR20cr+; NCR expansion: INR3-4cr; railway facility: INR30cr+ (commissioned); total capex for INR900-1000cr target: INR100cr (incl. inorganic)
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic growth (80-85% of INR900-1000cr target); INR50-70cr earmarked for strategic acquisition (geography/product agnostic); debt-equity capped at 0.6-0.8x; funding mix: partial equity, partial debt; no dividend policy mentioned
risks & watch-items: RDSO approval delays (6-12mo for field trials); Brazil market entry uncertainty; EU FTA impact delayed (3-6mo); ABS regulation (8% revenue exposure, factored in); China competition in US cables; European auto slowdown (mitigated by US/Mexico exposure); labor law complexity in Brazil
management quality / tone: Confident, strategic, and disciplined — emphasized long-term Remsons 2.0 transformation, export diversification, and margin expansion; avoided overpromising on Brazil/Astro; acknowledged delays in policy timelines; tone focused on execution, not hype
non-obvious takeaways: INR60cr CV order is first major win in commercial vehicles — signals expansion beyond two-wheelers; BEE Lighting order from German OEM is design-led, low-volume manufacturing — not mass production; railway products (air brake, slack adjuster) have export potential but require RDSO — first-mover advantage in India; defense revenue already INR10-15cr — underappreciated growth vector

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- 65-year engineering heritage Tier-1 supplier across five vehicle segments (Passenger Cars, Commercial Vehicles, 2/3-Wheelers, Agriculture, Locomotive & Rail) with 30+ global OEM partners and premium clientele including Aston Martin, Lamborghini, Jaguar and Ford GT via BEE Lighting.
- Transformed from a mechanical-only, largely 2-wheeler cable business with no strategic alliances (2019) into a platform spanning Mechanical, Sensors, Lighting, Locomotive and Defense across 2W/3W/4W/CV/Off-highway/Rail, with 8 plants (India + UK) and 4+ JVs/acquisitions (2027 snapshot).
- Largely EV-agnostic and fuel-agnostic product portfolio built as one integrated platform across three engineering disciplines: Mechanical (cable/pedal/linkage), Sensors (sense/compute/control) and Lighting (exterior/interior/LED).

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Leadership Transition] Rahul Desai (30+ years automotive manufacturing experience, 17+ years in CEO/senior leadership roles, former CEO & Executive Director at Pinnacle Industries and CEO at CIE India) succeeds Amit Srivastava as CEO effective September 4, 2026.
- [Group Structure] Corporate structure comprises Remsons India (cables, gear shifters, winches, pedals, CBS) and Remsons Holding UK (Remsons Automotive UK — cables/winches/pedal systems/jacks; BEE Lighting UK and BEE Lighting Czech Republic — lighting design/engineering), plus Aircom Remsons (tyre mobility), Remsons Edge Tech (Railways & Defense parts), Remsons-Uni Autonics (sensors & embedded systems) and Remsons Brazil.
- [Awards] Recognitions include Ford World Excellence Award (2020), Ashok Leyland Gold Quality & Best Supplier Award (2022), ACMA 1st Place HR and QC Competition awards (2023), Quality Forum India Gold Award for TQM/Kaizen (2024), and Great Place to Work certification with a Top-25 ranking in India's Best Workplaces in Manufacturing (2025).
- [Promoter/Listing] Promoted by Vishwa Prakash Harlalka and family; Remsons went public in 1995.
- [Industry Headwinds] Deck flags six sector-wide headwinds framing its strategic response: geopolitical issues, high inflation, EV transition, labour cost & shortage, trade wars, and input-cost volatility (crude, steel, copper).
